# Frontend design skill for distinctive production-grade interfaces

Curated by Skill Harbor — Cline's frontend-design skill: build distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Design thinking first — understand the context (purpose, audience, constraints), pick a bold aesthetic direction (brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic, luxury, playful, editorial, brutalist, art deco, soft pastel, industrial…), commit to it with precision, then implement real working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue) that is functional, striking and meticulously refined. Covers typography (beautiful, characterful fonts — never Arial/Inter/system fonts by default), color and theme (cohesive aesthetic, CSS variables, dominant colors with sharp accents), motion (CSS-first micro-interactions, high-impact orchestrated reveals), spatial composition (asymmetry, overlap, grid-breaking, generous negative space or controlled density), and atmospheric backgrounds (gradient meshes, noise textures, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, custom cursors). The "never" list: overused font families, clichéd purple gradients on white, predictable layouts, cookie-cutter design. Honest caveats: guidance only — the agent writes the code; overlaps with other design listings here (anthropics frontend-design variants, bencium-impact-designer, affaan-m-ecc-frontend-design) — same craft, different authors. Apache-2.0 licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
